note: Art direction for Hui Hai (HH1), chosen by the owner on 2026-09-27: the Hàng Trống folk painting 'White Tiger' (Bạch hổ), Hanoi, traditional design (public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:White_tiger_Hang_Trong.jpg). The owner's bar (2026-09-27): the cards must look like photos of the real old paintings in a museum, never like cute game or children's art. The Hui Hai are drawn as tiny spirit folk in leaf clothes, never as a picture of the Ba Na people.
style: A photograph of an authentic old Vietnamese Hàng Trống folk painting from Hanoi, in exactly the style of the reference image: woodblock-printed ink outlines hand-coloured with bright pigments on dó paper, a deep cobalt-blue ground with the uneven density of hand-brushed pigment, swirling cloud scrolls in pink, green, orange and yellow outlined in white, fur, grass and leaves drawn with many fine parallel brush strokes, slightly misregistered colour, a little fading and wear on the paper, the naive, stylised and slightly comic manner of Vietnamese folk painting. Faces are stylised the way the reference stylises its tiger: simple drawn features with a few ink lines, not realistic and not cartoon-cute. Use ONLY the style of the reference: do not draw a tiger or a cat, do not copy its composition. The Hui Hai are tiny forest spirits of Vietnam's Central Highlands, drawn much smaller than the ferns and pebbles around them, wearing clothes of woven leaves and fern fronds, never a picture of any real people or their dress. It must look like a museum photograph of a real, old, hand-painted original, the kind hung on a gallery wall, indistinguishable from the reference: the same hand, the same brush, the same pigments, the same age. The image is only the painted surface, filling the frame edge to edge: no wall, no frame, no label. NOT digital illustration, NOT a game or cartoon or anime or children's-book style, no big eyes, no cute or chibi faces, no glossy or airbrushed rendering, no 3D, no soft gradients, no bokeh. Absolutely no text, letters, Chinese characters, seals, stamps or watermarks.

families.Hui Hai: Background: the cobalt-blue ground and swirling many-coloured clouds of the reference, above a Highland forest floor of ferns, bamboo, moss and smooth river pebbles by a stream, all in the folk painting's flat stylised manner.

subjects.HH1-H01-kitten: the littlest Hui Hai: a tiny girl spirit in a dress of woven leaves, her hair in a tuft tied with a grass blade, pushing a smooth river boulder many times her size with both arms, among tall ferns.
subjects.HH1-H01-bigcat: the littlest Hui Hai: a tiny girl spirit in a dress of woven leaves standing on a round boulder in the middle of a forest stream, holding a pebble over her head in one hand, concentric ripples drawn in fine white lines around the boulder, fern fronds bowing on both banks.
subjects.HH1-D01: a Hui Hai of the stream: a tiny boy spirit in a cape of fern fronds crouched on a wet pebble in a rippling stream, flicking a splash of water at a small fish.
subjects.HH1-D02: Yă Hui Hai, Lady of the Ferns: a tiny old woman spirit with white hair in a bun, wrapped in a shawl of woven moss, resting in the coil of a giant unfurling fern frond, one hand on a large rock beside her.
subjects.HH1-D03: no figure: a forest path among ferns and bamboo, a single smooth pebble landing beside a pair of big straw sandals at the edge of the picture, and among the ferns only two small eyes peering out.
